explanation: The std::ratio class template in C++ provides a way to represent rational numbers (fractions) with numerator and denominator as compile-time constants. This enables compile-time calculations and type-safe rational arithmetic, which can be used for precise, zero-overhead computations in template metaprogramming. It is particularly useful for scenarios requiring exact rational representations without runtime overhead, such as unit conversions or compile-time constants.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of std::ratio to define rational numbers at compile time. It creates ratios for 1/2 and 1/3, then uses the template metafunction ratio_add to compute their sum at compile time. The resulting ratio's numerator and denominator are accessed via static members, illustrating how C++ templates enable compile-time rational arithmetic without runtime overhead. This showcases the power of modern C++ features for type-safe, zero-cost mathematical computations.
